label: input token v during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase
explanation: Token detector: fires on every step where the input is the letter v during the original phase, and on essentially nothing else (only 14 stray copy-phase activations on dev; never on the delimiter or on v fed back as an input during the copy phase). Magnitude is highest when v is the first token (t=0, often max activation) and falls with position. A repeated v is weaker than the first v in the sequence (the in_first condition keeps 93% of mass but only 80% of the lowest quartile). Sequence length L, neighbouring tokens and digit count have no effect on whether it fires.

issues: Minor wording issue: the explanation says the feature never fires on v when it is fed back during the copy phase. The stray copy-phase activations (14 on dev, 15 on test) are exactly that case. They happen at the first copy step, when the fed-back token is a v that began the sequence. They are tiny (0.00-0.02 of max) and carry 0.0% of activation mass, so this is noise rather than a systematic class.
Test scores are slightly below what was reported: precision 1.0, recall 0.99986, F1 0.99993, mass recall 0.999998. That is not exactly 1, but it is not meaningful either.

The other claims hold. Activations by phase are original 107877, delimiter 0, copy 14. Among in_tok values only v fires: 54% of v steps are active, which is the original-phase share, and no other token shows any activation. Activation mass falls steadily with orig_idx (0.203 at t=0 down to 0.009 at idx 8), while the firing rate stays at 0.033 at every orig_idx, as the explanation says. Adding in_first==1 on test gives mass recall 0.928 and lowest-quartile coverage 0.79, which matches the claimed 93%/80%. L and to_go have flat rates. There are 0 false positives.
